paragraphs: Peter's whole sermon points at one Man. David died and was buried, and his tomb "is with us to this day" (Acts 2:29). But God raised Jesus, because "it was impossible for death to keep Him in its grip" (Acts 2:24). That's why Peter can say that God has made Jesus "both Lord and Christ" (Acts 2:36), and why the Lord of everything is the One you can trust with your whole life, friend.

Now look at what the crowd does with that. They're cut to the heart, and instead of running, they ask, "Brothers, what shall we do?" (Acts 2:37). Peter's answer is as plain as a cookie recipe: "Repent and be baptized," and they'll receive forgiveness and the gift of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:38). Then he says, "This promise belongs to you and your children and to all who are far off" (Acts 2:39), and that includes you, baker, and it includes a worn-out stamper who got called out of a junk drawer.

And watch what happens next, because saving faith doesn't stay in a corner by itself. The believers devote themselves to the teaching, the fellowship, the breaking of bread and prayer (Acts 2:42). They share with anyone in need (Acts 2:45), and the Lord adds to their number daily (Acts 2:47). Nobody bakes a good batch alone, friend, and I would know, because I've got a whole bakery and it's way too quiet when nobody's passing the sprinkles.
